lines.en: She took us back here — to the place it all began.
She said having a familiar backdrop might make what’s about to happen a little less traumatic, but I disagree.
I think we’re screwed no matter what. And I think putting an end to things up here will do naught but manufacture one more reason for me to despise heights.
We learned along the way that’s really all the rooftop is, though. That it’s only important because we think it’s important. Because that’s how it was presented to us.
But if we’ve all existed all along, scattered throughout the city during those moments where it feels like there’s only one or two people left in the world, it really makes you think.
What else have I missed from keeping my sights set on one goal? Only offering passing glances at the conflicts that would insert themselves between this sky and me?
I imagine it’s a lot. No — I imagine it’s everything. And that I, too, have been living in a world of my own creation. That world just happens to exist within someone else’s.
It doesn’t make it any less real, though. Not to me, at least. And if I have come to accept Himawari as an unrealized fact, why stop there?
Because she’s tangible? Because I can reach out and play with her hair or adjust her ribbon on her way out the door?
It’s equally possible there’s some version of me running around between dimensions, trying to pull someone back to where I think they belong. I just haven’t encountered one yet.
And I hope for my sake (both old and new) that I don’t. For I’d have no kind words to say about anyone who leaves this girl’s side for more than a minute.
Yet here I am, about to leave her for, at minimum, fifteen years. And that’s assuming everything goes right. Which we both know it never does.

But if I am to leave this place one day, and wind up one layer closer to the world in which I can sit with her again, be it on some park bench or at the table just outside of my bedroom, know that I will not so easily part with it.
There’s a world in which I’m praying right now. Where this is all unfolding again because that’s simply just how fate works or something along those inexplicable lines.
And in that world, I hope my prayers are answered. That I find a way to keep her and preserve not just the only thing I have ever truly loved, but the only thing to ever believe in me.
So much so that she’d break the world just to give me a chance.
But in thinking that, I realize again that there are unseen parallels between her and something else I must part with.
And again, I wish for the parallels to end there.
I wish for a world where she won’t have to do this forever.
But can I really wish for another wish?
Or is this me just being too afraid to say goodbye?
: Hima-chan...what are you going to do exactly? Like...are you the one who chooses where we wake up or...where we’ll be when we do?
: Once again, you’re thinking I’m a lot greater than I actually am, Mom.
: That’s something this world chooses on its own. Without help from me. Or Shi-chan. Or the gods themselves. And it’s something we just have to live with.
: That’s...well, okay. I don’t really know what to make of that.
: It was confusing enough learning about a secret company that oversees religion and time and that gods are real to begin with. Now I have to accept that the world has a mind of its own too?
: Kinda figured that one would be an easier pill to swallow given how that other stuff is a lot less believable on a sheer conceptual level.
: To be fair, pretty much anything is believable on sheer conceptual level to me after meeting Big Boi.
: Hey, I know him! He’s in the same department as me! I’ll tell him you said hi if I bump into him again.
: Any other messages you’d like me to deliver? Perhaps to a spiteful or irritating god that’s appeared to you in a dream? Advertisements these days are so invasive, aren’t they?
: Can you deliver a message to your boss about a request to come visit you at least once per month so I don’t have to go back to living a life without my sunflower?
: God, I wish. That would make all of this a zillion times easier. But no, that could send the Wishing Well spiraling into chaos and set a bad precedent.
: You did it before when you took us to Aomori, though...
: With an illegally manufactured and unsanctioned dimension door, yeah. That was already confiscated, though.
: I’d need to make a brand new one. And even that wouldn’t be a reliable solution since the last one failed so dramatically.
: And you really can’t come back either?...
: I know I probably shouldn’t be saying this as your mother...but I completely endorse you breaking more of your company’s rules if it means-
: Hima-chan?! Where are you-
: There are no rules I wouldn’t break to spend another minute with you guys.
: I’d love to come back. Nothing would make me happier. Well...apart from you guys coming to me, that is.
: But I don’t think that can happen.
: But why? Why do you have to leave us again?
: Because I don’t exist yet. At least not in this timeline. And if we let anyone who’s anyone break the laws of the Wishing Well to go anywhere they want, no one would wish anymore.
: The more I appear to you here, the less likely it is that I’ll appear anywhere else.
: But that’s just what happens when you’re the product of two people who break every rule to give you life in the first place.
: I’m not only visiting to try and set you on the right path or convince you that Maya’s the root of all your troubles. I’m here because this is the world that brought the two of you together.
: And I’m sure I don’t need to spell out why that needs to happen in order for me to be born, right?
: You guys need something to fight for. Something to search for. Otherwise, you’ll grow complacent and the reasons for this world to exist will dwindle down to zero.
: Is something going to happen to you for coming here again?...
: Leave my problems to me. I can handle them so long as you guys play your part.
: But what happens if we fail?...
: We’ll all die. So yeah, no pressure at all.
: I guess for me it’s less “death” and more just never being born, though? I’m kind of a special case. That’s why I was chosen for this.
: Himawari-
: Time’s up, Dad.
: We need to say goodbye now.
: Take care of yourself, okay? I’m always worried about you feeling lonely.
: Then, once you’re home, we’ll open the greatest boba shop the world has ever known.
: These last four months have been the greatest of my life. You understand that, right?
: Yeah, I do. I tend to have that effect on people.
: Will you be able to do any of this anymore? Or is it really just in our hands now?
: That’s classified.
: Unclassify it. You’re not the only one who worries.
: Now why, in our final moments together, would I tell you something that would make you worry even more? Just let me handle it. My problems are simple, all things considered.
: So the next time I’ll see you is probably when you’re born then, huh?...
: Remember to name me after your favorite flower. I’ve built a good chunk of my persona around it.
: Will you be lonely in the meantime?
: I have friends. Don’t worry. They’ll keep me company while I brag more about how awesome my parents are.
: You might not have friends for long then. That sounds annoying.
: It is. I’m very annoying. And it’s probably all your fault too since you’re the one I grew up wanting to annoy.
: Please annoy me again some day. I’ll be looking forward to it.
: PlEaSe AnNoY mE aGaIn SoMe DaY. I’lL bE LoOkInG fOrWaRd tO iT.
: Yeah...that. Don’t change at all.
: That’ll be on you and Mom unfortunately. Kids are the result of their upbringing, you know. That’s probably why you suck so hard.
: You know me so well.
: Of course I do.
: I love you, Dad...
: I love you too...
: Do you ever wish you could stop the clock?...
: And live in a single moment for the rest of your life?
: Yeah...
: Do you feel that way right now?
: I do...
: Not embarrassed this time?
: Are you?
: A little. We don’t normally hug. It feels kind of weird.
: Then go hug your mother.
: She’ll want to say goodbye as well...
: You need to eat more than just ikura. Its health benefits come at the cost of high sodium and I don’t want you to develop hypertension. Okay?
: Okay, Mom.
: And make sure to do your homework now that you aren’t being home-schooled anymore. No more dead people for science fair. It doesn’t work. I’ve tried.
: I will succeed where you have failed. Mark my words.
: You’re probably right. Because you’re the smartest, most beautiful, most amazing girl the world has ever known. And I will think about you every second of every day.
: Please don’t. I know what you do in your free time.
: Hima-chan.
: It’s Dad. Dad is what you do in your free time.
: I love you so, so, so, so much. And I will be an even better mother once we meet again.
: Don’t kid yourself. You’re the best mother a girl could ever ask for. Being any better than that would just make you overbearing.
: Then I will be overbearing. And I will smother you with a love so powerful that you will have no choice but to grow and accept it.
: I’m looking foward to it. And I’ll be thinking of you every day.
: You’ve always been my role model. And I’ll keep working hard to be even half the woman you are when I grow up.
: Even though you are technically not a woman right now. And how I’m more used to hugging you than I am Dad, but it feels a little weird when we’re the same size.
: You might be taller than me some day, you know. You have your father’s genes as well.
: God, I hope not. Finding clothes would be a nightmare.
: It was! It was the only hard part of my life in Aomori! But we can go shopping together once we’re both freakishly tall!
: That’ll be a long time from now, but I’ll mark it down on my calendar. I’m sure it’ll be worth the wait.
: I won’t keep you waiting long, okay?! We’ll get out of here as fast we can! And you better be there with another home-cooked meal for us the second we do! I love you so much!
: I love you too, Mom...
: I’ll miss you more than you could ever imagine...
: That brings us to the end of the road, though. It’s finally time to say goodbye.
: And while it is sad, know that it won’t stay that way.
: It’ll get worse. Unbearable. You’ll feel trapped and scared and anxious and won’t know which way you’re supposed to go or what you’re supposed to do.
: When that happens, I want you to think of what makes you happiest. And let that be the light that guides you away from the darkness and back to me.
: You know exactly what I’ll be thinking of, Himawari.
: Stay strong. Even when the odds are stacked against you.
: Which they are, by the way. I can’t really undersell just how badly the world wants you to fail.
: Don’t worry. It’s still pretty evident even without your help.
: Are you ready then?
: Any last words?
: Quick questions you might have for a time-traveller?
How do we do this?
: So...what are we going to do exactly? Are you just going to disappear? Or-
: I figured we could do it the way you guys always do. Huddled together and hugging or touching like that changes anything.
: I’ve always thought that looked fun. And it might make you more comfortable since it’s something you’re familiar with?
: You’re saying we haven’t needed to do that?
: Nope. Doesn’t really change anything. The world will chew you up and spit you out wherever it wants you regardless of who you’re touching.
: It’s nice having someone so close for something so scary, though...right?
: Are you scared?
: Terrified, really.
: This is the most time I’ve gotten to spend with you in a very long while. And now it’s all about to go away.
: But I promise I’ll only cry a little. And I’ll try to keep a brave face since I know you’ll be working hard.
: Just do me a favor and try that as well, okay? Don’t be scared anymore. And face forward, always.
: Okay...
: Promise?
: Promise.
: Anything else you want to say?
Where will you go?
: Where will you go once Ayane and I are presumably sent back to a mostly-functional world?
: I have an idea. I’m afraid it’s classified, though.
: Of course it is. Like half of the things I want to know about you are classified.
: How’s it feel to care about somebody who never wants to open up, huh? Annoying, I bet.
: Is that a jab at your father in what could very well be one of the last sentences you ever speak to him?
: Could I really send you off without one last jab at your character? What sort of daughter would I be if I didn’t make you question your own behaviors?
: No, I get it. I just wish you wouldn’t hide things from me.
: Hey, you should be happy that I told you this much.
: If the world got what it wanted, you’d know nothing at all. And I probably wouldn’t exist at all.
: So call it good will or just an act of self-preservation or whatever it is you want to call it. The point remains that you know which direction to head in now.
: You just don’t know how long it will take to reach the end or what you’ll see when you get there.
: Anything else you want to ask?
What should I do about Maya?
: So...I know you said this is Maya’s wish. That it’s the world she created. But what does that mean for where I’m supposed to go from here?
: Like...how does just knowing that get me any closer to an answer at all?
: You think I’d be all vague if I knew the answer to that and not just directly tell you?
: Given how much you’ve classified so far...kind of?
: Fair enough. I really have no idea, though.
: Someone would have done something with her by now if we knew the answer to that question.
: I think if anyone is going to find the answer, though, it’s you.
: She’s your wish after all. She’s anything and everything you want her to be.
: So maybe the key is just...not wanting her anymore?
: Just an idea. I’m sure you’ll come up with your own soon enough.
: Anything else?
I’m ready (Leave Himawari)
: I can’t do it.
: You’re going to have to.
: No, I just can’t do it if you give me the choice. How am I supposed to leave you behind when you’re what I’ve been looking for this whole time?
: The same way I’m going to do that with you guys.
: Reluctantly. Miserably. Hesitantly. Any other adverb you want to toss in there that can’t begin to describe how painful this is for all of us.
: It’s what needs to be done, though. And it might hurt now, but one day...
: It will all be worth it.
: So lets all make a pact! That our next life together will be happier than this one!
: That we’ll vacation in Hokkaido every winter!
: That I’ll get better at skiing and Mom can spend every Christmas with us and her butler-dad!
: Aunt Sana and Aunt Ami can come too! And we’ll all live a perfect little life together, where there’s no fear of the unknown or the divine or anything else that governs and controls our lives.
: It’ll just be us. And we’ll just be happy. And all we’ll have left to fear is the rising price of sushi and state of the Japanese economy.
: It is at this point that I’d like to invite both of you to close your eyes.
: Close your eyes and imagine it.
: Imagine the world we’ll have together. So perfect. So pure.
: Where every morning will be filled with love and good food. And nights will be filled with cuddling and movies and...probably more good food!
: Then we’ll go to sleep and start over. Then sleep. Then start over! And it’ll keep going and going and going until that’s all we can remember!
: Hima-chan-
: Imagine it! Just imagine it, okay?!
: Because it won’t ever be real if you don’t...
: And I need it.
: I need you.
: I love both of you so much.
: And...
: I’m sorry.
: Hima-
: You’ll keep everything but me...
: That’s one memory you can’t take with you.
: WHY?!
: Because I’m an idiot! That’s why! I’m a terrible, horrible waste of a girl!
: It wasn’t supposed to happen like this! You weren’t supposed to wake up in Aomori!
: And we weren’t supposed to spend the best four months of our lives in a sandbox I made to cope with how much I miss you! Don’t you understand?!
: You said it yourself! How are you supposed to live without me?!
: How are you supposed to make it back to your reality and function knowing that I am lost without you?!
: HIMAWARI???
: I’m sorry, Mom...That I have to put you through this again.
: But you can be happy now...losing the memory of losing me at all.
: You won’t need Dad’s help to keep going. You won’t have any dreams about me. You can fight and move forward and do all the things that I would only hold you back from!
: SSSSTOPPPPPPPP!!!!
: It’s too late for that...
: This is all my fault for being too reckless. For wanting to see you too much.
: So now I will bear the heavier burden of that and you won’t need to feel any guilt at all over something you had nothing to do with.
: I’ve dragged the two of you into an unforgivable tragedy. This is simply my penance.
: But it’s okay...because soon, the two of you can go back to existing without the constant fear of your daughter-
: WON’T...FORGET!
: You have to!
: You think you can just take a shortcut to happiness?! That my mistake is enough to carry you from who you are now to who you’ll be for me?!
: That’s something you have to do on your own! No amount of meddling is going to fix that, no matter how much I want it to!
: LETTTTTGO!!!!
: And lose you forever?! No! This is what needs to be done for me to see you at all! Stop fighting it!
: TRUST....YOU....
: THIS TIME.....TRUST....YOU....
: You mean it?...
: DAUGHTER...
: TRUST...
: I’ll make it up to you one day...
: I’ll make it up to both of you one day...
: But for now, just know that I love you.
: And that I wouldn’t be doing this at all if I had a choice.
